en.headline: Hong Kong airport offers free sunflower lanyards for hidden disabilities
en.dek: Passengers with non-visible conditions can pick up free lanyards at five customer service centres so staff know they may need extra time or support.
body: Hong Kong International Airport has joined the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower programme, allowing passengers with non-visible disabilities or conditions to signal discreetly that they may need additional time, patience or assistance.

The Airport Authority said free sunflower lanyards are available at five designated customer service centres across Terminals 1 and 2. More than 80 per cent of frontline staff have received training to recognise the symbol and offer appropriate support without requiring passengers to explain their condition.

The programme is voluntary. Passengers do not need to disclose medical details or provide documentation. A sensory corner near Gate 10 is also open to anyone with sensory needs, whether or not they wear a sunflower symbol.

The initiative began in September and forms part of the airport’s wider accessibility efforts. Staff are instructed to offer help with queues, clearer information or a quieter approach when they see the symbol.

zh.headline: 香港國際機場免費提供向日葵掛繩支援隱性障礙旅客
zh.dek: 有非可見殘障或狀況的乘客可在五個顧客服務中心免費領取掛繩，讓職員知道他們可能需要額外時間或協助。
body: 香港國際機場已加入隱性障礙向日葵計劃，讓有非可見殘障或健康狀況的旅客可低調顯示他們可能需要多一點時間、體諒或協助。
機場管理局表示，向日葵掛繩在一號及二號客運大樓共五個指定顧客服務中心免費提供。逾八成前線職員已接受培訓，見到標誌會提供適切支援，旅客毋須解釋自己的狀況。
計劃屬自願性質，旅客無需披露醫療詳情或出示證明。10號閘口附近的感官角落亦開放予有感官需要的人士使用，不論是否佩戴向日葵標誌。
計劃於九月開始，是機場加強無障礙服務的一部分。職員獲指示，見到標誌時可在排隊、提供更清晰資訊或較安靜的處理方式上給予協助。
